title: Composition Pasting Coherence
statement:
Let $B$ be a commutative ring and use the derived constant-$B$ strict-tower operations and normalized proper/open comparisons $\gamma$, open comparisons $\beta$, and proper-square mates $E$ of [def-cbc-strict-constant-tower-operations, def-cbc-strict-tower-open-extension, lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus]. Let $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow hZ$ be separated finite-type morphisms of schemes with a supplied compatible tower [lem-cbc-compactifiable-compatible-tower]
$$X\xrightarrow a\overline X\xrightarrow p\overline Y\xrightarrow qZ,\qquad Y\xrightarrow i\overline Y.$$
Here $U=\overline X\times_{\overline Y}Y$ has projections $b:U\hookrightarrow\overline X$, $p_Y:U\to Y$, and $c:X\hookrightarrow U$, with $bc=a$, $p_Yc=f$, and cartesian square $Q=(b,i,p_Y,p)$. The displayed open maps are quasi-compact and $p,q,p_Y$ proper. Put $F_f=R_{p_Y}^{\mathcal T}J_c$, $F_h=R_q^{\mathcal T}J_i$, $F_{hf}=R_{qp}^{\mathcal T}J_a$. On towers whose $n$-th evaluations are restrictions of finite-coefficient bounded-below etale-origin complexes [def-cbc-finite-constant-coefficient-transport],
$$D=R_q^{\mathcal T}\gamma_QJ_c:F_hF_f\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{hf}$$
is a natural isomorphism, using the canonical proper-direct-image and open-extension compositors [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition].
For two such towers indexed by $1,2$, let a refinement from $1$ to $2$ consist of proper maps $u:\overline Y_1\to\overline Y_2$, $v:\overline X_1\to\overline X_2$, $w:U_1\to U_2$, satisfying $ui_1=i_2$, $va_1=a_2$, $wc_1=c_2$, $vb_1=b_2w$, $p_2v=up_1$, $p_{Y,2}w=p_{Y,1}$, $q_2u=q_1$. Define the three refinement maps $C_f,C_h,C_{hf}$ by $\gamma$ for the squares $(c_1,c_2,1_X,w)$, $(i_1,i_2,1_Y,u)$, $(a_1,a_2,1_X,v)$, followed by the corresponding proper direct images. Then the actual strict-tower transformations satisfy
$$C_{hf}D_2=D_1(C_hF_{f,1})(F_{h,2}C_f).$$
For a base change $g:Z'\to Z$ and its pullbacks $g_Y,g_X$, let $e_f:G_{g_Y}F_f\to F_f'G_{g_X}$, $e_h:G_gF_h\to F_h'G_{g_Y}$, and $e_{hf}:G_gF_{hf}\to F_{hf}'G_{g_X}$ each be the proper mate followed by the open comparison. The vertical interchange identity is
$$e_{hf}(G_gD)=(D'G_{g_X})(F_h'e_f)(e_hF_f).$$
Consequently $D$ and this identity transport unchanged through the above refinement maps and through any common refining compatible tower. These equalities hold before evaluation, with canonical composition identifications inserted.
